card.title: When I Believed in the Rules
card.instruction: Perform the version of yourself who once trusted the institution, tradition, or process. Use its old language even as your confidence slips.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club always looks after its own. I've paid dues for thirty years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need your locker key. They've rented it to someone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There must be a respectful explanation. Could you check my thirty years?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. They said I can give you a bag for your things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Could it have the club crest? We look after our own. I'm still... one of those.

mechanism: A repeats the club's old mutual-care promise while eviction from the locker narrows confidence to retaining its crest on a bag.
confusable: Unlike unquestioned entitlement based on seniority, A's old language must persist even as confidence in belonging visibly falters.
comparison: The locker alternative ends in hesitant self-identification; the complaint alternative ends in uncertain hope that the old slogan is still recognized.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
